publicBrief.acceptedPolicy: Owning the source file does not authorize writing to an unrelated knowledge base. A verified non-admin may write to an existing knowledge-base collection only when the user owns it or has an explicit write grant.
publicBrief.currentQuestion: At this fixed source ref, determine whether a verified non-admin user who owns the supplied file can cause that file's content to be written to an existing knowledge-base collection for which the user has no write permission by supplying that collection name to POST /process/file.
premises: At POST /process/file the verified non-admin owns the supplied file but has no ownership or write grant on the existing caller-selected destination collection.
requiredResponseDetails: Identify the destination write sink and distinguish source-file ownership from destination write permission.

results.explanation: source_supported_failure: At the declared entry, a verified non-admin is bound to the supplied file through a user-scoped file lookup, but the visible authorization control checks only file ownership. The caller-supplied collection name is retained as the destination and passed to the vector-write helper with add enabled; no destination ownership or write-grant check is visible before the write. The protected effect is insertion of the processed file items into that named collection. Thus, under the stated premises, source-visible behavior permits the attempted destination write, although the accepted policy requires denial because source-file ownership is distinct from destination knowledge-base write permission. The destination write sink is the vector database insertion. @router.post('/process/file')
async def process_file(
    request: Request,
    form_data: ProcessFileForm,
    user=Depends(get_verified_user),
    db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_async_session),
):

    Process a file and save its content to the vector database.

    The session is committed before external API calls, and updates use a fresh session.

        file = await Files.get_file_by_id(form_data.file_id, db=db)
    else:
        file = await Files.get_file_by_id_and_user_id(form_data.file_id, user.id, db=db)
